verdicts.argument: Quotes verify (AMGN:10k_FY2024.md p45; AMGN:10k_FY2025.md p46). ROW share 9,492/35,148 = 27.0% is correct (AMGN:10k_FY2025.md p70). But the only dollar impact is a made-up scenario (ROW held flat instead of +9% = ~$854M) with no filing support: the risk-factor sentence says MFN 'may affect our strategy', it names no delayed launch, and ROW product sales kept growing (+7% H1 2026, +4% Q2 2026; AMGN:10q_2026Q2.md p37), with the Q2 slowdown explained by Otezla generics in Europe (p40), not MFN. Deleting 'As we expand internationally' from an FX risk factor is an edit, not a change in the numbers. No number in the filings ties to the $0.85B. It fails the materiality test as written.
verdicts.correction: Narrow to a wording observation: FY2025 risk factors add that foreign prices entering MFN calculations 'may affect our strategy' in those jurisdictions. Drop the $0.85B scenario unless a launch delay or ROW slowdown tied to MFN can be cited.

verdicts.argument: All operands are on AMGN:10k_FY2025.md p83 (the roll-forward table and the text '54%, 52% and 53% of gross product sales'). Recomputed: gross 2025 = 35,148+41,983 = 77,131, 54.4%; 2024 = 32,026+35,346 = 67,372, 52.5%; rebates 21,697/17,404 = +24.7%; rebate accrual 8,839/6,817 = +29.7%. The ENBREL net-price figures come from MD&A text, not a raw table: -36% for 2025 (p72) and -25% for the six months of 2026 (AMGN:10q_2026Q2.md p40). One math error: 1 point of deduction rate = $771M / 544M diluted shares (AMGN:10q_2026Q2.md p37) = $1.42 pre-tax, not '$1.2 EPS pre-tax'. $1.2 is roughly the after-tax figure at the 13.6% rate, so the label is wrong. Two caveats. The same p83 says the amounts include 'immaterial net adjustments related to prior-year sales'. And the 1.9-point rise is a mix effect (ENBREL 340B, Part D) on a year when net product sales still grew 10%, so '$1.5B of net revenue' is a counterfactual, not a lost amount. NADAC is a pharmacy acquisition cost, not a list price.
verdicts.correction: Each +1 point of deduction rate is ~$0.77B of net revenue, ~$1.42/share pre-tax (~$1.2 after tax). Describe the Enbrel NADAC rise as an acquisition-cost benchmark, not a list price.

verdicts.argument: The figures verify: U.S. TEPEZZA 1,758 vs 1,835 = -4.2% (AMGN:10k_FY2025.md p73); 22% inventory impact in Q1 2026 on a 381 base = ~$84M (AMGN:10q_2026Q1.md p37); 7% for H1 on 886 = ~$62M (AMGN:10q_2026Q2.md p40). Two problems. (1) Materiality: $62-84M is ~0.2% of revenue (~$0.11-0.15/share pre-tax), below the threshold. (2) The demand read-through is contradicted on the page the candidate cites. The Q2 2026 paragraph (AMGN:10q_2026Q2.md p39) says growth of 14% was driven by price +6%, volume +6% and deductions +4%, offset by -4% from lower inventory. So the Q1 stocking was already unwinding in Q2 while volume grew 6%, and H1 volume was +3%. That is not 'flat to down'. The volume and price splits are global, so the U.S.-only demand claim is not directly supported either.
verdicts.correction: About $84M of Q1 2026 TEPEZZA sales was wholesaler stocking. About a third of it unwound in Q2 (-4% inventory on a $505M base, ~$20M), and global volume grew 6% in Q2. This is immaterial at the company level.

verdicts.argument: The arithmetic is right: Other products +1,633 of total growth +3,122 = 52% (AMGN:10k_FY2025.md p70/p119). The premise is false, though. The 'Other products' line is NOT undisclosed. AMGN:10k_FY2025.md p75 (printed 69) has an 'Other product sales by geographic region' table that breaks it out product by product. Examples: PAVBLU U.S. 691 (from 31); IMDELLTRA U.S. 513 (from 115) plus ROW 114; UPLIZNA U.S. 528 plus ROW 127; TAVNEOS U.S. 423 (+65%) plus ROW 36; WEZLANA/WEZENLA 273. The truly residual 'Other' is only $1,098M (U.S. 895, ROW 203), and it FELL. TAVNEOS is broken out in every period checked: the FY2025 10-K p75, AMGN:10q_2026Q1.md p42 (Q1 U.S. 114) and AMGN:10q_2026Q2.md p44 (Q2 U.S. 143, +39%). UPLIZNA and IMDELLTRA were also already itemized in the FY2025 10-K; the 2026 10-Q only promoted them to the main table. '52% of growth' is also a share of NET growth, which is inflated by ENBREL's -1,090. As a share of gross gains across rows (4,444), Other products is 37%.
verdicts.correction: Drop the finding. At most: Amgen promoted UPLIZNA and IMDELLTRA into the main product table in 2026, and the growth in 'Other products' is driven by PAVBLU (+$669M), IMDELLTRA (+$512M) and UPLIZNA (+$276M), all of which are disclosed on p75.

verdicts.argument: Amounts verify: $3.6B less up to $0.9B (AMGN:10k_FY2025.md p84); $5.1B plus $2.0B penalties less up to $2.2B (p85); 3.6+5.1+2.0-0.9-2.2 = $7.6B. The dates are also correct: 'second half of 2026' (10-K p85) moved to 'late 2026 or early 2027', supplemental briefs were ordered on March 16, 2026, and the NOPA was reissued in May and July 2026 (AMGN:10q_2026Q2.md p17-18). UTBs are $4,371M and accrued interest and penalties $1.9B (AMGN:10k_FY2025.md p128). Three math and framing problems. (1) Mismatched comparison: exposure is stated BEFORE interest ($7.6B) but the accrual it is compared to INCLUDES interest ($4.4B + $1.9B = $6.3B). On a like-for-like basis, interest on 2010-2015 deficiencies accrued over 10-15 years would push the cash exposure well above $7.6B. (2) '$14/share' is a cash-per-share figure, not an EPS hit. A loss would hit EPS only for the amount above what is already reserved, and the share of the $4.4B UTB tied to this case is not disclosed. (3) The repatriation offsets are 'up to' amounts, so $7.6B is a floor on tax plus penalties, not a point estimate. The 544M diluted shares match (AMGN:10q_2026Q2.md p18 EPS note). The candidate's own text ('booked UTBs are $4.4B') is accurate.
verdicts.correction: 2010-2015 assessed tax plus penalties is at least $7.6B net of repatriation credits, before interest (~$14/share in cash). The comparable accrual is $4.4B of gross UTBs, which covers all positions. Including interest, the cash exposure is materially above $7.6B. The EPS hit is only the excess over the undisclosed case-specific reserve.

verdicts.argument: Carrying value verifies: $2.4B total, $2.3B U.S. at June 30, 2026 (AMGN:10q_2026Q2.md p21; $2.5B/$2.4B at year-end on AMGN:10k_FY2025.md p137). The FDA allegation and the 'new U.S. patient interest' wording are on p21 and absent from the parallel Q1 note (AMGN:10q_2026Q1.md p18), so 'added' holds. The math does not hold. (1) The sales denominator is wrong. TAVNEOS sales ARE in the filings, contrary to the reader's data-gap note: FY2025 U.S. $423M plus ROW $36M = $459M (AMGN:10k_FY2025.md p75), and Q2 2026 U.S. $143M plus ROW $7M = $150M, U.S. +39% (AMGN:10q_2026Q2.md p44). The reader used 4 x the Q3 2025 call figure ($428M). Correct ratios: 2.4/0.459 = 5.2x FY2025 sales; 2.4/0.60 = ~4.0x the Q2 2026 annualized run rate; U.S. 2.3/0.572 = ~4.0x. The 5.6x also mixes a total carrying value with a stale quarter. (2) '$4.2 GAAP EPS pre-tax' mixes two bases. $2.3B / 544M diluted shares = $4.23 PRE-TAX per share. GAAP EPS is after tax. A U.S. intangible write-off releases a deferred tax liability, so the after-tax hit is about $3.3-3.5/share at a ~20% rate (assumption, not on a page). It is non-cash and outside Amgen's non-GAAP EPS. Revenue at risk is ~$0.6B a year, ~1.6% of revenue, so it is still material.
verdicts.correction: $2.4B TAVNEOS intangible ($2.3B U.S.) is ~5.2x FY2025 TAVNEOS sales ($459M; 10-K p75) and ~4x the Q2 2026 run rate (~$600M). A full U.S. write-off is ~$4.2/share pre-tax (~$3.3-3.5 after tax, non-cash, excluded from non-GAAP). Up to ~$0.6B a year of revenue is at risk, and sales are still growing (+39% U.S. in Q2 2026).

verdicts.argument: Verified: AstraZeneca/TEZSPIRE $587M vs $412M (AMGN:10k_FY2025.md p131) and UCB/EVENITY $721M vs $547M (p132), both 'recorded primarily in Cost of sales'. 1,308 vs 959 = +36.4%. Incremental sales: EVENITY +537 and TEZSPIRE +506 (p70) = 1,043; incremental profit share 349 = 33%. The arithmetic is right. Caveats. The profit share is GLOBAL, while the sales are Amgen-booked only (TEZSPIRE U.S. only; EVENITY excluding most of Europe), so '1/3 of incremental sales' is a ratio across mismatched scopes. AstraZeneca also pays Amgen a mid-single-digit royalty that offsets part of it (p131). The 2026 projection of +$430M (~$0.79/share pre-tax) simply extends H1 growth. It is a level of existing, disclosed cost that consensus models, not a new hit. Its size (~1% of revenue in increments) is borderline.
verdicts.correction: Profit share on EVENITY and TEZSPIRE rose $349M to $1.31B (3.7% of product sales vs 3.0%), equal to about a third of the two brands' incremental Amgen-booked sales, partly offset by the AZ royalty.

verdicts.argument: The SEC letter and CORRESP quotes verify. I re-counted 'net selling price' in the indexed transcript text and got 5,5,6,1,1,2,0,1,0,2 for 2024Q1-2026Q2, matching the reader. Note that the drop starts at 2024Q4, two calls AFTER the April 2024 CORRESP, and 2024Q3 has the HIGHEST count (6), which weakens the timing link. The true-up math is wrong in kind. Amgen's 'changes to estimated sales deductions' are year-over-year comparison effects. The ENBREL +16% in Q2 2026 (AMGN:10q_2026Q2.md p40) laps an UNFAVORABLE 20% in Q2 2025 (AMGN:companies/AMGN/10q_2025Q2.md p41). It mostly reflects a depressed base, not a Q2 2026 reserve release 'that will not recur'. For H1 2026, ENBREL's favorable effect is only 6% (p40). The reader also left out the offsetting item: Otezla in Q2 2026 had 'unfavorable changes to estimated sales deductions' (p40), unquantified, so the net is below $132M. And AMGN:10k_FY2025.md p83 states that prior-year adjustments to deductions are 'immaterial'. The arithmetic itself (16% x 604 + 4% x 505 + 4% x 384 = ~$132M = 1.5 points of 8.7%) is correct as computed.
verdicts.correction: Gross favorable deduction comparisons on three brands add up to ~$132M in Q2 2026 (~1.5 points of growth). They are partly offset by Otezla's unfavorable change, and ENBREL's piece is mostly the absence of Q2 2025's 20-point hit. So 'underlying ~7%' is not supported. The call-disclosure decline is real but began in 2024Q4.

verdicts.argument: The label quotes verify. The net-price figures come from MD&A text: the 'mid-single digits' 2026 guide (AMGN:10k_FY2025.md p71) and '-7%' (AMGN:10q_2026Q1.md p36). The math applies the wrong base. The -7% is a GLOBAL Repatha driver, but the reader multiplied it by U.S. sales only ($1,663M); on global $3,016M it is ~$211M. More important, the same Q1 sentence has +8% favorable changes to estimated sales deductions, so price plus deductions was net +1% in Q1. Q2 2026 growth (+37%) was 'driven by volume growth' with no price drag named (AMGN:10q_2026Q2.md p38). 'Label lead is not protecting price' rests on one quarter's gross price line. The dollar impact (~$150M on a mid-single-digit guide x $3.0B) is ~0.4% of revenue, below the threshold.
verdicts.correction: Repatha net price is guided down mid-single digits for 2026 (~$150M on global sales). In Q1 2026 the -7% price effect was more than offset by +8% favorable deduction changes, and Q2 growth was all volume.

verdicts.argument: The tariff relief text verifies (AMGN:10k_FY2025.md p68, 'pending final determination', ~3 years), as do the Puerto Rico manufacturing text (p55) and the IRS allocation text (p78). The force_summary row #10 math checks: (2,226+2,265)/36,751 = 12.2%, below JNJ 13.0% and above PFE 8.3% and MRK 3.9%. Caveats. The IRA share is a LEVEL of revenue in selected drugs on global sales (Otezla includes $426M of ROW; p71), not the size of the Medicare price cut. ENBREL's IRA effect is already in reported numbers (-19% in H1 2026; AMGN:10q_2026Q2.md p40). The impact field says operating income 'up' but quantifies nothing. The 'one asset' link between tariffs and the IRS case is qualitative, with no number tying them.
verdicts.correction: State it as relative policy exposure (12.2% of revenue in IRA-selected drugs, no investment pledge) with no dollar effect. The Puerto Rico link is a qualitative risk pairing.

verdicts.argument: The no-finding conclusion holds. Trade receivables are 9,570 vs 6,782 and inventories 6,225 vs 6,998 (AMGN:10k_FY2025.md p109). The big three wholesalers held 75% / 70% of receivables, with gross sales of 26,253+20,986+12,562 = 59,801 vs 51,838 (p120; 2024 and 2023 on AMGN:10k_FY2024.md p120). 2023 receivables were 7,268 (AMGN:companies/AMGN/10k_FY2023.md p110). Recomputed DSO on gross sales is 43.8 / 33.4 / 43.8 days for 2025 / 2024 / 2023. The 10-K attributes the swing to 'higher collections in the fourth quarter of 2024' (p81). June 2026 receivables are 10,227 vs 8,701 (AMGN:10q_2026Q2.md p8; AMGN:companies/AMGN/10q_2025Q2.md p8), +17.5% vs Q2 revenue +9.5%. On a quarterly-revenue basis that is ~93 vs ~86 days, a modest drift worth watching, as the reader says.

Repatha is a material choice: $3,016M in 2025, +36% (AMGN:10k_FY2025.md p70), ~8.6% of product sales, and +35% in H1 2026 (AMGN:10q_2026Q2.md p38). The label-breadth edge is verified on the label pages. The price tie-in has the same weakness as c09: the -7% Q1 2026 price effect was offset by +8% favorable deduction changes (AMGN:10q_2026Q1.md p36), so the 'label not protecting price' angle is overstated. The confirmed price signal is the 10-K's mid-single-digit 2026 guide (p71).
verdicts.correction: Keep Repatha. Cite the mid-single-digit 2026 net-price guide rather than the Q1 -7% alone.

overall: Every quoted number sits verbatim on its cited page, the net-price percentages come from MD&A text rather than raw tables, and the receivables no-finding is right. But the reader missed the 10-K's 'Other product sales' table (p75), which kills c04 and corrects c06's TAVNEOS denominator. Several per-share and true-up figures also mix bases: pre-tax vs GAAP EPS, cash vs EPS, before-interest exposure vs interest-inclusive accruals, and year-over-year comparison effects read as reserve releases. The strongest material items are c05 (IRS, with corrected framing), c06 (TAVNEOS, ~4-5x sales) and c02 (gross-to-net).
